the use of MRN assisted transmission outperforms both direct transmission and FRN assisted transmission, and is very promising for future vehicular communication systems.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MRNs can provide significant QoS improvement to VUEs under co-channel interference, and MRN assisted transmission can be a promising candidate for future mobile communication systems.
, for a VUE served by an RN under moderate to high penetration loss, it is better to let it be served by a MRN rather than an FRN or directly by a BS.
, for vehicular users, the use of moving relays can be a promising solution for improving their QoS, especially when vehicular penetration is high.

the use of MRN is more beneficial to serve VUEs in a multi-cell environment with co-channel interference.
